node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Read given condition order
node.description: Identify which event is being conditioned on in statements such as probability of A given B.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Condition as filter
node.description: Interpret the given event as a filter that restricts the sample space before calculating probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Denominator from given event
node.description: Choose the count or probability of the given event as the denominator in a conditional probability calculation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Numerator is joint condition and target
node.description: Choose the count or probability satisfying both the given event and the target event as the numerator.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conditional ratio from restricted counts
node.description: Calculate a conditional probability as favourable outcomes within the restricted sample space divided by the restricted total.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Formula intersection numerator
node.description: Interpret the numerator P(A and B) in the conditional probability formula as the intersection of the target and given events.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nonzero given event check
node.description: Check that the given event has nonzero probability before using a conditional probability formula.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Row condition from table
node.description: Calculate a conditional probability from a two-way table when the given event is represented by a row total.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Column condition from table
node.description: Calculate a conditional probability from a two-way table when the given event is represented by a column total.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare reverse conditionals in a table
node.description: Compare P(A given B) and P(B given A) in a two-way table by using different denominators.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Second branch as conditional probability
node.description: Interpret a second-stage branch probability in a tree diagram as conditional on the first-stage outcome.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Joint probability from tree path
node.description: Use a complete path in a tree diagram to find the joint probability of a sequence of events.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conditional from tree joint ratio
node.description: Recover a conditional probability from a tree diagram by dividing a relevant joint path probability by the probability of the given event.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Update probability after information
node.description: Revise a probability estimate when new information restricts the possible outcomes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare conditional to marginal probability
node.description: Compare a conditional probability with the corresponding marginal probability to judge whether information changes likelihood.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Independence check from a two-way table
node.description: Use conditional and marginal probabilities from a two-way table to decide whether two events appear independent.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Define events in conditional word problems
node.description: Define target and given events clearly before setting up a conditional probability calculation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Natural frequency Bayes table
node.description: Use natural frequencies in a table to organise base rates, true positives, false positives and posterior probabilities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Base rate partition
node.description: Partition a population by prior categories before applying conditional probabilities in a Bayes context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Posterior probability interpretation
node.description: Interpret the reversed conditional probability after observing evidence in a Bayes context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Diagnostic test false positive context
node.description: Model contexts where a positive result can arise from both true positives and false positives.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conditional probability reasonableness check
node.description: Check whether a conditional probability answer is reasonable by comparing it with the restricted sample space, marginal probabilities and context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conditional numerator satisfies both events
node.description: The numerator in a conditional probability count must satisfy both the target event and the given event.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conditioning event must be possible
node.description: A conditional probability is defined only when the given event has nonzero probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Second tree branch is conditional
node.description: A later branch in a tree diagram is interpreted in the context of the earlier branch outcomes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bayes reverses condition with base rates
node.description: Bayes reasoning uses base rates and conditional evidence probabilities to estimate a reversed conditional probability.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Given event order reversed
node.description: Learner reads P(A given B) as if A is the condition and B is the target event.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conditional ignores base rate
node.description: Learner estimates a reversed conditional probability from test accuracy or evidence likelihood alone, ignoring the base rate.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Independence means mutually exclusive
node.description: Learner treats independent events as if they cannot happen together, confusing independence with mutual exclusivity.

edge.rationale: Reading the order of target and given events directly practises given-event language.
Choosing the given-event denominator directly practises restricted sample-space reasoning.
Row-condition calculations are a core form of table-based conditional probability.
Second-stage branch interpretation is central to tree-diagram conditional probability.
Natural-frequency tables are a common way to practise Bayes reasoning.
Given-event language builds on interpreting event statements and compound event wording.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify target and condition events in a probability statement.

edge.rationale: Conditional filtering builds on the idea of restricting a sample space in compound events.
edge.failure_signal: Learner continues to use the original sample space after a condition is given.

edge.rationale: The given-event denominator follows from treating the condition as the restricted sample space.
edge.failure_signal: Learner divides by the original total rather than the condition total.

edge.rationale: After selecting the restricted denominator, the numerator must satisfy both the target and condition.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts all target outcomes rather than target outcomes inside the condition.

edge.rationale: The restricted count ratio uses the joint numerator over the given-event denominator.
edge.failure_signal: Learner forms a ratio with numerator or denominator from the wrong sample space.

edge.rationale: The formula numerator uses the intersection of the target and given events.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses union instead of intersection in the conditional probability formula.

edge.rationale: Checking nonzero probability depends on understanding valid probability values and endpoints.
edge.failure_signal: Learner divides by zero or treats an impossible given event as conditionable.

edge.rationale: Row-condition calculations rely on selecting the row total as the condition denominator.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the grand total for a row-conditioned probability.

edge.rationale: Column-condition calculations are parallel to row-condition calculations with a different denominator orientation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot switch denominator orientation when the condition is a column event.

edge.rationale: Comparing reverse conditionals requires calculating conditionals with different denominators.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes P(A given B) and P(B given A) must match.

edge.rationale: Second-stage tree conditionals build on updating branch probabilities after prior outcomes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats all second-stage branches as unconditional probabilities.

edge.rationale: Joint path probabilities are found by multiplying probabilities along a complete path.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds branch probabilities along a tree path.

edge.rationale: Recovering a conditional probability from tree paths depends on identifying joint probabilities first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a joint probability directly as a conditional probability without normalising by the condition.

edge.rationale: Updating probabilities after information is the practical effect of conditioning on a restricted sample space.
edge.failure_signal: Learner ignores new information when estimating probability.

edge.rationale: Comparing conditional and marginal probabilities checks whether new information changed likelihood.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot decide whether conditioning changed the probability.

edge.rationale: Independence can be checked by comparing conditional probabilities with marginal probabilities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies independence from event labels rather than probability comparison.

edge.rationale: Word-problem setup requires identifying which event is target and which event is given.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates a reverse conditional or an unconditional probability from the wording.

edge.rationale: Bayesian base-rate partitioning is used to reason about reversed conditionals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses a conditional without accounting for different group sizes.

edge.rationale: A natural-frequency Bayes table begins by partitioning the population using base rates.
edge.failure_signal: Learner fills evidence counts without first splitting the base population.

edge.rationale: Posterior interpretation follows from reading the reversed conditional from the natural-frequency table.
edge.failure_signal: Learner interprets a likelihood as the posterior probability.

edge.rationale: Diagnostic-test contexts require separating true positives from false positives in a natural-frequency model.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats every positive result as a true positive.

edge.rationale: Reasonableness checks compare the answer against the restricted sample space and context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts a conditional probability that is inconsistent with the restricted counts or context.
